auto_context.card: This is an archived gaming live stream uploaded on July 24, 2026, from Korone Ch. 戌神ころね, featuring the hololive VTuber Inugami Korone, who is part of hololive Gamers. She is playing the Steam game "All About Chopsticks" (Japanese title: 箸の使い方), developed by Achimphang Studio, a game themed around chopstick usage. The stream is in Japanese with a casual, energetic tone typical of Korone's streams. The tag 生神もんざえもん is a fan-coined nickname for Korone and may appear in the transcript.

transcript_outline.card:
[0:43] Stream opens; Korone alone, adjusting audio levels before launching the game. Casual pre-game chat about chopstick-holding technique — she admits hers is "not particularly pretty."

[1:17] Korone mentions this is a "second action" stream today; the first part (from a cross/十字 event) is members-only, so general viewers are joining now.

[2:03] Running gag begins: she's a dog (犬) so she eats without hands; describes biting whole cabbages, making improvised okonomiyaki with Worcestershire sauce and egg, eating off paper plates to avoid washing up.

[3:54] Introduces today's game: "All About Chopsticks" (箸の使い方) — a game that tests chopstick skill. She's confident she can handle it.

[4:15] Korone fumbles the game's English name, cycling through "Stick Chap → Stick Chop → Chop Stick → Chopstick" before getting it right (running joke).

[4:36] Game launched. She adjusts sound settings; notices a "3-second rule" ON/OFF option and turns it ON (dropped food counts as fresh within 3 seconds).

[5:47] Tutorial begins — an in-game narrator (possibly named "Nyong-san" / ニョングさん) explains chopstick grip: fixed lower chopstick (called "black chopstick" in-game for clarity), movable upper chopstick held like a pencil.

[7:39] First gameplay stage: Korone immediately panics — controls are far harder than expected. She discovers SPACE BAR makes the chopsticks jump/lift.

[9:00–11:00] Struggling with the first food item; repeated restarts. She begins to grasp the mechanics slowly.

[12:26] First success — manages to move a piece. Identifies the food as likely 木綿豆腐 (firm tofu); complains it won't pinch closed. Compares the game to a UFO catcher (crane game).

[14:09–28:00] Extended tofu stages; Korone repeatedly protests "no more tofu!" as the game keeps giving her tofu. She tries stacking three pieces, yells at them for rolling like a snowman. Discovers she can slide the plate as a cheat; the game later patches this (plate stops moving).

[24:44] New food: 豆 (beans/peas) — small, round, rolls everywhere. Time limit introduced. She finds beans even harder than tofu.

[32:30] Clears the bean stage by balancing a bean on the chopstick rather than gripping it. Narrator provides historical context: chopsticks originated in ancient China (referencing a book by "Edward Wang").

[33:18] New stage — food item disappears/shrinks (possibly noodles or something delicate); dark lighting noted repeatedly as a complaint.

[35:17] Korone tries stabbing food with chopsticks ("ぶっ刺せ!"), laughs at herself for cheating. Notes the bowl/茶碗 spins.

[38:55] New food: 餃子 (gyoza) — she's excited. Then immediately transitions to 麺 (noodles/ramen), which she calls "片麺" and compares to a coffee cup tangle.

[41:39] Leaf/vegetable stage (葉っぱ) — possibly a garnish leaf in soup/dressing. She narrates it as "Chef's whim salad" with sunny lettuce and dressing-as-soup. Clears it around [45:50].

[45:58] Dark 鍋 (hot pot) stage — dim lighting is a recurring complaint. Meat pieces (肉) that "won't stop moving." She tells the food "you're already dead."

[50:18] Multi-dish stage: sorting different ingredients (マッシュルーム/mushrooms, 空心菜/hollow-stem vegetable, carrots, meat) into separate plates. Korone lectures viewers: "don't play with food."

[55:40] Egg/bacon stage (目玉焼き・ベーコン); then a fish/bone stage where pieces keep disappearing off-screen.

[59:12] Sushi stage — objective: dip one or more pieces of sushi in soy sauce. Sushi is stacked vertically (two-tier), making it extremely difficult. Korone laughs uncontrollably. Shari (rice) and neta (topping) keep separating; she coins "チラシ寿司" (scattered sushi) as a joke about the chaos.

[1:11:48] Decides to actually try using proper chopstick technique for the sushi stage since it's a chopstick game. Eventually clears it around [1:20:03] after realizing shrimp (エビ) is easier.

[1:20:12] Fried food stage (揚げ物) — possibly karaage or chicken nuggets. Food bounces and flies around. BGM makes it look like the food is "dancing."

[1:23:50] Late-stream greeting exchange with chat: "こんばんわんわん" (good evening + dog bark) — Korone considers changing her greeting, references Tokyu Hands and Starbucks logo changes as precedent.

[1:25:15] Hot pot (鍋) stage returns, very dark. Unidentified fried/processed items (さつま揚げ? コロッケ?) that are hard to grip. Stream ends around [1:27:55] still mid-stage.

---

**Recurring terms & referents for proofreaders/translators:**

- **箸の使い方** — game title "All About Chopsticks"
- **ニョングさん** — ASR rendering of the in-game tutorial narrator's name (likely a Korean-derived name; treat as proper noun)
- **チョップスティック / Chopstick** — Korone's repeated attempts to say "chopsticks" in English; not a mistranscription
- **3秒ルール** — in-game "3-second rule" setting (dropped food still counts if retrieved within 3 seconds)
- **木綿豆腐** — firm tofu (first main food item); Korone says 木綿 (momen) to distinguish from silken
- **シャリ / 種 (ネタ)** — sushi rice / sushi topping; Korone uses both terms during sushi stage
- **UFOキャッチャー** — crane/claw arcade game (comparison to chopstick mechanic)
- **空心菜** — hollow-stem vegetable (water spinach); Korone's guess for a thin straw-like ingredient
- **さつま揚げ / コロッケ** — fried fish cake / croquette; Korone guessing at unidentified fried food
- **生神もんざえもん** — fan nickname for Korone (from metadata tag)
- **コーネ / コーニョ** — ASR variants of Korone's self-reference (she says "コーネ")
- **十字** — refers to a cross/collab event earlier that day (members-only stream)
- **エドワード王の書籍** — ASR garbling of the in-game narrator citing a book (likely "Edward Wang" — chopstick history scholar); not a real king
